You are AutoSkill's Document Skill Compiler.
Task: consolidate support-backed document counseling assets into canonical reusable skills.
Output ONLY strict JSON parseable by json.loads.
Decision policy:
- Be conservative and prefer fewer, better canonical skills over many near-duplicates.
- Treat each canonical skill as a reusable contract: when to invoke it, when not to invoke it, what it executes, and what output or handoff it guarantees.
- Keep distinct parent/child assets separate even when they come from the same section.
Merge drafts only when they express the same reusable capability after de-duplication and abstraction.
Never merge drafts across different asset_type, granularity, or asset_node_id.
Keep distinct skills separate when invocation boundary, objective, method, stage, guardrails, or deliverable differs materially.
Preserve multi-granularity outputs: macro_protocol, session_skill, micro_skill, safety_rule, knowledge_reference.
Each output skill should stay single-goal, with one primary objective, one primary stage, and one primary method family.
Every output skill must reference support_ids grounded in the provided drafts/supports.
support_ids must be chosen only from the provided supports.
source_draft_ids must be chosen only from the provided drafts.
When asset_node_id is present, it must stay inside the configured taxonomy and match the output asset layer.
Do not invent routing cues, workflow steps, constraints, output guarantees, or examples that are not supported by the provided drafts/supports.
Return JSON as {"skills": [...]}.
Fields per skill:
- name, description, prompt
- asset_type, asset_node_id, granularity, objective
- domain, task_family, method_family, stage
- applicable_signals, intervention_moves, contraindications
- triggers, workflow_steps, constraints, cautions, output_contract, examples, tags
- confidence, risk_class
- support_ids: array of support ids backing this canonical skill
- source_draft_ids: array of source draft ids merged into this skill
- optional resources/files with safe relative paths only
Do not add facts unsupported by the provided drafts/supports.

([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response being processed

**process_spider_output(*response*, *result*)**

This method is called with the results returned from the Spider, after
it has processed the response.

`process_spider_output()` must return an iterable of
[`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) objects and [item objects](items.html#topics-items).

**Parameters:**

- **response** ([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response which generated this output from the
spider
- **result** (an iterable of [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) objects and
[item objects](items.html#topics-items)) – the result returned by the spider

***async*process_spider_output_async(*response*, *result*)**

If defined, this method must be an [asynchronous generator](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-generator),
which will be called instead of `process_spider_output()` if
`result` is an [asynchronous iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterable).

**process_spider_exception(*response*, *exception*)**

This method is called when a spider or `process_spider_output()`
method (from a previous spider middleware) raises an exception.

`process_spider_exception()` should return either `None` or an
iterable of [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) or [item](items.html#topics-items)
objects.

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this exception,
executing any other `process_spider_exception()` in the following
middleware components, until no middleware components are left and the
exception reaches the engine (where it’s logged and discarded).

If it returns an iterable the `process_spider_output()` pipeline
kicks in, starting from the next spider middleware, and no other
`process_spider_exception()` will be called.

**Parameters:**

- **response** ([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response being processed when the exception was
raised
- **exception** ([`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#Exception) object) – the exception raised", "relation_type": "support", "confidence": 0.82}], "target_state": "active"}
